publisher: Pew Internet & American Life Project and Elon University
report: The Future of the Internet II

entries.label: A global, low-cost network thrives
entries.quote: By 2020, worldwide network interoperability will be perfected, allowing smooth data flow, authentication and billing; mobile wireless communications will be available to anyone anywhere on the globe at an extremely low cost.
entries.subject: global low-cost mobile network

entries.label: English displaces other languages
entries.quote: In 2020, networked communications have leveled the world into one big political, social and economic space in which people everywhere can meet and have verbal and visual exchanges regularly, face-to-face, over the internet. English will be so indispensable in communicating that it displaces some languages.
entries.subject: English as the dominant online language

entries.label: Autonomous technology is a problem
entries.quote: By 2020, intelligent agents and distributed control will cut direct human input so completely out of some key activities such as surveillance, security and tracking systems that technology beyond our control will generate dangers and dependencies that will not be recognized until it is impossible to reverse them. We will be on a "J-curve" of continued acceleration of change.
entries.subject: autonomous technology beyond human control

entries.label: Transparency builds a better world, even at the expense of privacy
entries.quote: As sensing, storage and communication technologies get cheaper and better, individuals' public and private lives will become increasingly "transparent" globally. [...] Looking at the big picture [...] this will make the world a better place by the year 2020. The benefits will outweigh the costs.
entries.subject: transparency versus privacy
entries.note: Quote shortened with [...] to fit 400 characters.

entries.label: Virtual reality is a drain for some
entries.quote: By the year 2020, virtual reality on the internet will come to allow more productivity from most people in technologically-savvy communities than working in the "real world." But the attractive nature of virtual-reality worlds will also lead to serious addiction problems for many, as we lose people to alternate realities.
entries.subject: virtual reality productivity and addiction

entries.label: The internet opens worldwide access to success
entries.quote: By 2020, this free flow of information will completely blur current national boundaries as they are replaced by city-states, corporation-based cultural groupings and/or other geographically diverse and reconfigured human organizations tied together by global networks.
entries.subject: internet and national boundaries
entries.note: The scenario opens with a reference to Thomas Friedman's The World is Flat and the idea that the internet lets individuals collaborate and compete globally; the quote keeps the predictive sentence.

entries.label: Some Luddites/Refuseniks will commit terror acts
entries.quote: By 2020, the people left behind (many by their own choice) by accelerating information and communications technologies will form a new cultural group of technology refuseniks who self-segregate from "modern" society. Some will live mostly "off the grid" [...] while others will commit acts of terror or violence in protest against technology.
entries.subject: anti-technology refuseniks and violence

notes: Seven agree/disagree scenarios for 2020, all captured. Skipped: one question asking respondents to rank spending priorities (no named year, no agree share). Non-random sample; no margin of error.
